case.summary: An analyst request flagged transaction 3660108 on card C05061-K1 during an investigation into multi-card losses without shared devices. Investigation confirmed a burst of three unauthorized online product-C charges totaling $2,189.02 between 2017-01-12 and 2017-01-14. All three transactions were conducted from new devices (D009708 and D009709) operating behind an anonymous proxy. Peer analysis identified the identical operational signature across cards C07212-K2 and C11543-K2, with C07212-K2 linked to organized fraud ring 34603052. The activity was confirmed as card-not-present fraud using new devices, resulting in card blocking, case creation, cross-card monitoring, and regulatory reporting.

sar.narrative: This suspicious activity report details an organized card-not-present fraud scheme affecting customer C05061 and payment card C05061-K1, along with connected cards C07212-K2 and C11543-K2. Between January 12, 2017, and January 14, 2017, three unauthorized online product-C transactions totaling $2,189.02 were charged to card C05061-K1. The unauthorized activity comprised transaction 3660106 for $850.28 on January 12, transaction 3660107 for $890.79 on January 13, and transaction 3660108 for $447.95 on January 14. All transactions occurred in the online channel and were routed through billing regions 492 and 264 utilizing devices identified as new to the account. Transactions 3660106 and 3660108 were conducted via device D009708 with the profile RCT6303W87M7 Build/MRA58K on Windows 7 with Internet Explorer 11.0 desktop. Transaction 3660107 was conducted via device D009709 with the profile RCT6303W87M7 Build/MRA58K on Windows 10 with Internet Explorer 11.0 tablet. Both devices connected through an anonymous IP proxy to obfuscate the perpetrator's origin and identity. The abrupt high-value product-C charges completely deviated from the cardholder's historical profile, which showed zero product-C transactions over the prior sixty days. Graph analytics identified an identical attack pattern occurring simultaneously across cards C07212-K2 and C11543-K2, which each suffered multiple high-value product-C charges from new devices behind proxies. Furthermore, peer card C07212-K2 is linked to fraud ring 34603052 with nineteen confirmed fraud closed cases. The bank has blocked card C05061-K1, placed connected cards on automated monitoring, and submitted this report regarding the coordinated $2,189.02 fraud episode.

stop_reason: The investigation concluded under policy section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.885, surpassing the decisive threshold of 0.85 supported by multiple independent evidence bases including anomalous cardholder behavior, proxy-masked new devices, and cross-card links to known fraud ring members, meaning further investigative steps would not alter the decision.
